record.context_brief: spectral sequence interpretation of the algebraic transfer
record.original_question: Can the bigraded algebraic transfer tau^{*,*} be realized as the edge homomorphism of a spectral sequence in a way that gives a sensible measure of how far tau^{*,*} is from being an isomorphism of bigraded algebras?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 Can τ*,* be viewed as the edge homomorphism of some spectral sequence?
This problem is not so well posed, but the point would be to find some sensible way to measure the failure of τ*,* to be an isomorphism of bigraded algebras.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ denote the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra and let $\mathbb{F}_2$ be the field with two elements. For each integer $k\ge 0$, let $P_k=\mathbb{F}_2[x_1,\dots,x_k]$ be the polynomial algebra on $k$ generators in degree $1$, regarded as a left $A$-module via the standard action of the Steenrod algebra on the mod-$2$ cohomology of $(B\mathbb{Z}/2)^k$. The general linear group $GL_k=GL_k(\mathbb{F}_2)$ acts on $P_k$, commuting with the $A$-action. W. Singer's algebraic transfer is a homomorphism of bigraded algebras
$$\tau^{*,*}:\bigoplus_{k\ge 0}\mathbb{F}_2\otimes_{GL_k}\bigl(P_k\bigr)^{A}_{*} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ext}_A^{*,*}(\mathbb{F}_2,\mathbb{F}_2),$$
where the source is the direct sum over $k$ of the $GL_k$-coinvariants of the subspace of $A$-annihilated elements of $P_k$ (with appropriate degree shift), and the target is the cohomology of the Steenrod algebra. The transfer is known not to be an isomorphism in general.

Question: Does there exist a (multiplicatively structured) spectral sequence converging to $\mathrm{Ext}_A^{*,*}(\mathbb{F}_2,\mathbb{F}_2)$ as a bigraded algebra such that $\tau^{*,*}$ arises as its edge homomorphism, in such a way that the higher pages and differentials of the spectral sequence provide a meaningful measure of the failure of $\tau^{*,*}$ to be an isomorphism of bigraded algebras?
artifact.status_search_result: No spectral sequence realization of the Singer algebraic transfer as an edge homomorphism appears in the literature. Recent work (2025) on the Singer transfer focuses on Singer's monomorphism conjecture (now known to fail in some bidegrees) and on computational methods, without addressing the spectral-sequence interpretation problem. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Computational Approaches to the Singer Transfer
status_evidence.snippet: systematic, algorithmic method ... computing the preimage of elements under the transfer
status_evidence.claim: Recent research focuses on computational/preimage methods, not on spectral sequence realizations.

status_evidence.title: The Negation Of Singer's Conjecture For The Sixth Algebraic Transfer
status_evidence.claim: Singer's monomorphism conjecture is now known to fail; the spectral-sequence interpretation problem is distinct and not addressed.

status_evidence.title: On May spectral sequence and the algebraic transfer
status_evidence.snippet: On May spectral sequence and the algebraic transfer
status_evidence.claim: Existing work relates the transfer to known spectral sequences (e.g., May), but no edge-homomorphism realization for tau^{*,*} itself has been established.
